stem: A researcher is studying the Fas receptor, a cell-surface protein that triggers the extrinsic apoptosis pathway when bound by Fas ligand expressed on cytotoxic T cells.  In an experiment, cancer cells that escaped elimination by the immune system were found to produce soluble Fas proteins that did not promote apoptosis.  These proteins were shorter than the membrane-bound receptors and lacked the transmembrane domain.  DNA sequencing of these cells revealed no FAS gene mutations.  Which of the following is the most likely explanation for the formation of altered Fas proteins in these cancer cells?​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌​​​‌​‌​‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌​​​‌​​​​​‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌
explanation:
The cancer cells in this experiment produce a shortened, soluble form of the Fas receptor despite having no mutations in the FAS gene.  This is most likely due to alternative splicing, which allows a single gene to produce different protein isoforms without changing its DNA sequence.

During pre-mRNA processing, the spliceosome removes introns and joins exons.  Alternative splicing changes which exon sequences are retained in mature mRNA; this normal process contributes to tissue-specific expression of protein variants and is orchestrated by regulatory proteins that influence splice-site selection.

Cancer cells can evade immune-mediated killing in part through altered splicing of pre-mRNAs encoding proteins involved in apoptosis.  Normally, Fas ligand on cytotoxic T cells binds cell-surface Fas receptors and activates the extrinsic apoptosis pathway.  Skipping the exon encoding the Fas receptor's transmembrane domain produces a shorter, soluble receptor that cannot anchor to the cell membrane and transmit an apoptotic signal.  Soluble Fas can also bind Fas ligand, reducing its availability to activate membrane-bound receptors and further promoting resistance to apoptosis.

(Choice B)  Polyadenylation adds a poly(A) tail to the 3′ end of an mRNA transcript, supporting nuclear export, transcript stability, and efficient translation.  Defective polyadenylation can reduce protein expression but would not explain exclusion of the sequence encoding the transmembrane domain.

(Choice C)  DNA methylation is an epigenetic modification that generally suppresses transcription when present at gene promoters.  It can reduce FAS expression but does not directly explain production of a shorter receptor lacking a specific domain.

(Choice D)  Polycistronic mRNA, common in bacteria, contains multiple protein-coding regions that are translated into separate proteins.  Human mRNAs are generally monocistronic.  Polycistronic organization would not explain the production of different Fas isoforms.

(Choice E)  Ubiquitination is the process in which ubiquitin tags are attached to proteins, which can target them for proteasomal degradation.  This can reduce receptor abundance but does not explain synthesis of a soluble Fas isoform lacking the transmembrane domain.

Educational objective:Alternative splicing allows a single gene to produce different protein isoforms by changing which exon sequences are retained in mature mRNA.  Exclusion of the exon encoding the Fas receptor's transmembrane domain produces soluble Fas, which can inhibit Fas-mediated apoptosis and help cancer cells evade immune-mediated killing.​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌​​​‌​‌​‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌​​​‌​​​​​‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌
